editorial:
You follow Dr. Steven Murphy, a heart surgeon whose clean suburban life starts to crack when Martin, a quiet teen with a grudge, pushes into his home. At first it feels like awkward dinners and strange favors, but soon Steven's kids get sick in a way no doctor can explain. The movie turns a family drama into a cold, tense guessing game about blame, guilt, and impossible choices, and every scene makes you wonder what Martin really wants.

The acting is strong, especially Barry Keoghan as Martin and Colin Farrell as Steven, and the flat, eerie style keeps you uneasy without loud jump scares. It is slow and weird, so if you want fast action you may get restless; if you like dark puzzles, it sticks with you long after the credits. For the best picture, stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or pick up the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final stretch, Martin's curse forces Steven to make a terrible choice: kill one family member or watch them all die. Steven ties his wife and children in the basement, blindfolds himself, spins with a rifle, and shoots Bob. Bob dies, and the rest of the family slowly recovers. The last scene shows the surviving family at a diner while Martin watches, proving the debt is paid.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark psychological thrillers and strange family dramas.
